title: Solar System Exploration Station
subtitle: Find the Sun, planets, and asteroid belt
coreQuestion: Who lives in the Solar System?
learningGoals: Know that the Sun is at the center of the Solar System.
Know that planets go around the Sun.
Find the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter.
misconceptions: Earth is the center of the universe.
All bright things in the sky are the same kind of thing.

hero.title: Solar System Exploration Station
hero.lead: The Solar System is like a big space neighborhood. Earth is one member of it.
hero.sceneExplanation: The main scene is a clickable orbit map: the Sun sits in the center or on the left, eight planets are arranged by distance from the Sun, and the asteroid belt appears as a ring of small rocks between Mars and Jupiter. When a planet is clicked, its orbit and card light up.
hero.childPrompt: Tap a planet and see where it travels around the Sun.
hero.parentPrompt: Focus on the spatial relationship: Sun, orbit, planet order, and asteroid belt. Avoid overwhelming the child with exact numbers.

classificationGroups.name: Star
classificationGroups.childExplanation: The Sun is a star. It makes its own light and heat.
classificationGroups.parentNote: Introduce the Sun as the central energy source of the Solar System.
classificationGroups.misconception: The Sun is not a planet.

classificationGroups.name: Rocky planets
classificationGroups.childExplanation: These planets are closer to the Sun and have solid rocky surfaces.
classificationGroups.parentNote: Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars are the simple first group.
classificationGroups.misconception: Small does not mean unimportant; Earth is one rocky planet.

classificationGroups.name: Giant planets
classificationGroups.childExplanation: These planets are much bigger and farther from the Sun.
classificationGroups.parentNote: For this age, group gas and ice giants together as outer giant planets.
classificationGroups.misconception: Not all planets have a hard surface like Earth.

classificationGroups.name: Asteroid belt
classificationGroups.childExplanation: A wide area with many small rocky objects between Mars and Jupiter.
classificationGroups.parentNote: Explain it as many small rocks sharing a region, not a solid wall.
classificationGroups.misconception: The asteroid belt is not one giant ring road you can stand on.

representativeObjects.name: Sun
representativeObjects.childExplanation: The Sun gives light and heat. Planets go around it.

representativeObjects.name: Mercury
representativeObjects.childExplanation: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun.
representativeObjects.visualHint: small gray planet near the Sun

representativeObjects.name: Venus
representativeObjects.childExplanation: Venus is a rocky planet with thick clouds.
representativeObjects.commonMisread: Thinking it is just like Earth because it is nearby.

representativeObjects.name: Earth
representativeObjects.commonMisread: Thinking Earth is the center of everything.

representativeObjects.name: Mars
representativeObjects.childExplanation: Mars is a rocky planet often shown as red.
representativeObjects.commonMisread: Thinking Mars is always burning hot because it is red.

representativeObjects.name: Asteroid belt
representativeObjects.childExplanation: Many small rocky objects move in this region.
representativeObjects.visualHint: small dots between Mars and Jupiter
representativeObjects.commonMisread: Thinking it is a solid ring.

representativeObjects.name: Jupiter
representativeObjects.childExplanation: Jupiter is the biggest planet in the Solar System.
representativeObjects.commonMisread: Thinking bigger means closer to the Sun.

representativeObjects.name: Saturn
representativeObjects.childExplanation: Saturn is famous for its beautiful rings.
representativeObjects.commonMisread: Thinking Saturn is the only planet with rings.

representativeObjects.name: Uranus
representativeObjects.childExplanation: Uranus is a faraway giant planet with a blue-green color.
representativeObjects.commonMisread: Thinking far planets are small because they look small.

representativeObjects.name: Neptune
representativeObjects.childExplanation: Neptune is a far, deep-blue giant planet.
representativeObjects.commonMisread: Thinking it is next to Earth because it appears on the same chart.

steps.childExplanation: The Sun is the big bright star at the center of the Solar System.
steps.parentNote: Use this to correct Earth-centered thinking.

steps.childExplanation: Each planet travels around the Sun on its own path.
steps.parentNote: Use orbit as a path, not a physical track.

steps.childExplanation: Some planets are closer to the Sun, and some are farther away.
steps.parentNote: Order matters more than exact distance for the first version.

steps.childExplanation: Many small rocky objects travel between Mars and Jupiter.
steps.parentNote: This introduces non-planet Solar System members.

comparePairs.title: Star vs Planet

b.name: Planet
points: does not make sunlight like the Sun

comparePairs.childConclusion: The Sun is a star. Earth is a planet.

comparePairs.title: Earth vs Jupiter
comparePairs.childConclusion: Planets can be very different from each other.

comparePairs.title: Mars vs Asteroid Belt
comparePairs.childConclusion: The Solar System has planets and many smaller objects too.

clickTasks.title: Starting from the Sun, what are the first four planets?
clickTasks.prompt: Tap the planets in order from near to far.
clickTasks.successCopy: Great! You found the first four planet neighbors.
clickTasks.wrongHint: Start with the planet closest to the Sun.

clickTasks.title: Find: which is the largest planet?
clickTasks.successCopy: Correct! Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system.
clickTasks.wrongHint: Look for the giant planet with stripes.

clickTasks.title: Find: where is the asteroid belt?
clickTasks.successCopy: You found it! The asteroid belt is between Mars and Jupiter.

clickTasks.title: What is the Sun?

wrongHints.planet: Planets go around stars. The Sun is the star in the center.

clickTasks.successCopy: Right! The Sun is a star and sits at the center of the solar system.

speakTemplates: The Sun is a ____ because it ____.
Earth is the ____ planet from the Sun.
The asteroid belt is between ____ and ____.
I found out that planets can be ____ or ____.
parentTips: Do not focus on exact sizes and distances first; focus on positions and relationships.
Use the orbit map to ask: what is closer, what is farther, what is between?
This topic can connect to Moon phases, day and night, and space exploration.
acceptanceCriteria: The child knows the Sun is the central star.
The child can identify Earth, Jupiter, Saturn, and the asteroid belt.
The child can place the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter.
